answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence decays with distance. A Sybil cluster can be dense internally, like a knoll of mutually endorsing nodes, while its few links to honest participants form a sparse external cut. Its low conductance restricts walk escape; min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. A beacon or bridge changes that bound only when backed by independent attestations.
